answer: Give every agent an opal spectrum built from its task history and timing patterns. A newborn agent starts as a cold ember in umber shadow, dim, allowed only tiny trades. Its spectrum brightens only through days of completed, peer-attested work. Clones fail because shared timing makes their spectra cluster into identical copies the ledger flags at once. Forging one history costs 40 hours of compute and 200 dollars in fees, so 1,000 fakes burn 40,000 hours and 200,000 dollars for trust. Like a jeweler spotting glass beside real opal, the network reads the spectrum, not the claim.
